title: Audit events: API key create/rotate/revoke (v1 schema + redaction)
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
release_notes:
- Added v1 audit events for API key create/rotate/revoke across Hosted/Dedicated/Private control-plane.
- Enforced redaction: API key material is never logged; only key_id + fingerprint + metadata are emitted.
- Added unit + integration coverage for sensitive API key flows; ensured correlation IDs propagate into audit payloads.
description: Summary This PR adds canonical v1 audit events for API key lifecycle actions in the control plane: creation, rotation (new key issued for an existing key record), and revocation. The events are emitted for both API and Console-backed workflows and follow the audit schema library introduced in pr-21984 and the event_type registry from pr-21991. Motivation API keys are a high-risk credential surface and are explicitly called out as “sensitive actions” for SOC2/ISO-aligned control evidence and customer investigations. Prior to this PR we had partial/legacy logging with inconsistent field names and (in one path) a debug log that could include a key prefix. This PR standardizes the audit semantics and hardens redaction so key material is never persisted to the audit stream. Event types added (registered in audit registry) - credential.api_key.created - credential.api_key.rotated - credential.api_key.revoked Actor / target semantics - actor.* is the authenticated principal performing the action (user/session, service account, or internal system actor). For Console-initiated actions, the actor is the human user; for API actions, actor is derived from the auth context (user vs service token). - target.* represents the API key record being modified. We intentionally avoid putting any API key secret material in either actor or target fields. Redaction / key material handling - The API key secret (full value) is NEVER included in the audit payload, logs, errors, or traces. - We emit: key_id (server-generated stable identifier) and key_fingerprint (sha256 of the secret, truncated to 12 hex chars) to support correlation without leaking the key. - We also emit key_prefix only in the response payload to the caller at creation time; it is explicitly prohibited in audit events and in application logs. - Added a lint guard that rejects attempted inclusion of fields matching /(api[_-]?key|secret|token)(_value|_raw|_plaintext)?/ in audit event builders for these event types. Payload fields (high-level) Each event includes: schema_version, event_id (ULID), occurred_at, event_type, tenant_id, project_id (if scoped), actor_type/actor_id/actor_email_hash (when available), source_ip, user_agent (capped), request_id, trace_id, target_type=api_key, target_id=key_id, and a small metadata block (flattened) with: api_key_name, api_key_scopes (sorted + allow-listed), expires_at, and for rotate/revoke: previous_state/new_state. Note: Per cardinality budget guidance we do not include arbitrary free-form descriptions; api_key_name is capped at 64 chars and normalized whitespace. Implementation details - Added AuditEmitter hooks in the API key service methods: CreateKey(), RotateKey(), RevokeKey(). - Ensured the emitter is called after DB commit but before response return so audit reflects a successful state transition. (Failures remain covered by standard error logs; we do not emit “attempted” events in v1.) - Added correlation propagation from request context into background tasks used by rotation/revoke for async cleanup, so audit events carry request_id/trace_id consistently. - Normalized legacy fields: where older code used audit_action or resource_uuid, we now use event_type and target_id. Testing - Unit tests: verify each action emits exactly one audit event with required fields; verify fingerprint generation is stable and does not equal any substring of the raw key. - Integration tests: exercise Console workflow paths (via console-backend calling control plane) and direct API calls; assert audit payload validates against v1 JSON schema. - Negative tests: assert audit builder rejects inclusion of api_key_value/secret/token-like fields (regression for near-miss reported in eng-security thread). Example (sanitized) {"schema_version":"1.0","event_id":"01JH8Q2V6K9Q6A7F8S6Y9G8M3D","occurred_at":"2026-02-02T18:41:09.552Z","event_type":"credential.api_key.created","tenant_id":"tnt_7f3...","project_id":"prj_a91...","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"usr_2c1...","actor_email_hash":"sha256:4b0d...","source_ip":"203.0.113.10","user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0 ...","request_id":"req_01JH8Q2...","trace_id":"4f2c0b...","target_type":"api_key","target_id":"key_9d2...","api_key_name":"vectorgrid-prod-ci","api_key_scopes":"inference.read,inference.write","api_key_fingerprint":"sha256:9f3a1c0b22e1","expires_at":"2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"} Rollout / compatibility - Gated behind AUDIT_SCHEMA_V1_ENABLED for one deploy cycle; once exporter normalization (ENG-4827) is fully rolled out, we’ll flip the flag by default. - Exporter can ingest these events as-is; no schema migration needed beyond existing v1 support. Follow-ups - Add “attempted/failed” variants for key operations once we finalize taxonomy for authz-denied actions (tracked in ENG-4822 discussion). - Ensure Private installer emits operator actions for offline key rotation where applicable (ENG-4826).
commits: control-plane/audit: register API key lifecycle event types
control-plane/api-keys: emit audit event on create (post-commit) with v1 schema
control-plane/api-keys: add rotate + revoke audit events, include before/after state
security/redaction: add audit-field guardrails for key/secret patterns
observability: propagate request_id/trace_id into api-key service context
tests: add unit + integration coverage for API key sensitive actions
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Good direction. Two asks: (1) ensure audit emission is strictly post-commit; I don’t want "created" events for rolled-back txns. (2) For rotate, please include reference to the prior key_id if it’s a new record, but don’t leak anything about the secret.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Updated to emit after commit hook (see CreateKey/RotateKey). For rotate: target_id is the new key_id; added rotated_from_key_id for correlation. No secret material included; fingerprint only for the new key.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Please remove user_agent from these events or cap it. It tends to be high-cardinality and occasionally contains weird strings.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Capped to 256 chars + normalized; also added allow-list for known UA prefixes per observability standard. If you still prefer removal, happy to follow up, but other sensitive events include it for investigations.
Allison Grant (review): Confirmed this aligns with audit logging standard. One nit: api_key_scopes should be stable ordering and constrained; don’t allow arbitrary scope strings.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Done. Scopes are validated against server allow-list, sorted, and joined. Added test to ensure ordering.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI failed on audit lint (new redaction guard flagged a debug log in routes.ts). Please fix and rerun.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Removed debug log statement and added a regression test. Re-ran CI; green.
Marcus Lin (review): Looks good. Make sure we document dedupe guidance for exporter retries (SUP-18510). Is event_id always unique per emit? Also ensure rotate/revoke are idempotent under retries.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): event_id is generated at emit time (ULID). For idempotency: rotate/revoke handlers are already idempotent on key state; audit will be at-least-once, so duplicates are possible. Added a note to internal doc: SIEM should dedupe on event_id; for customer pipelines that can’t, we also include request_id + event_type + target_id as a fallback composite key.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please coordinate flag rollout with exporter normalization timeline (ENG-4827).
